thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Burn-rate alert: `Hosted API / chat+completions (streaming)`
- SLO: Availability (success rate) 99.90% / 30d
- Burn rate: 14.2x (1h), 6.1x (6h)
- Regions: us-east-1 (primary), eu-west-1 (elevated)
- Top error classes: 5xx spike + `stream_disconnect_server` increasing
Dashboards:
- SLO Overview: https://grafana.redwood.dev/d/slo-hosted-overview?tier=hosted
- Streaming Health: https://grafana.redwood.dev/d/streaming-health?route=/v1/chat/completions
Runbook: https://confluence.redwood.dev/display/ONCALL/Error+Budget+Exhaustion+Response+Runbook
(reactions: :eyes: x6)

Aisha Bello: ack, I’m on. Seeing the same on #eng-sre burn summary. 1h window is ugly.
Quick check: this looks like mostly us-east-1 + specific model? anyone already scoped by `model` label?

Amara Diallo: gateway side: 5xx are predominantly upstream timeouts (504) + a chunk of 499s but those are client aborts. streaming disconnect classifier shows `server_disconnect` jumped starting ~10 min ago.
I’m looking at: https://grafana.redwood.dev/d/gw-errors?region=us-east-1&route=/v1/chat/completions

Peter Holtz: infra/oncall: queue depth + GPU util are pegged in us-east-1. This smells like overload + cascading timeouts.
We’ve got the protective throttling flag ready (Hosted only). Question is do we flip it now vs try routing failover first.

Mina Haddad: routing: can shift a portion of Hosted traffic to us-west-2 and eu-central-1, but west is already ~70% capacity.
Also: Dedicated pools look fine; I don’t want any global action that touches Dedicated.

Ravi Menon: agree. If we do throttling, scope to Hosted tier only and only to streaming route(s). Keep Dedicated isolated.
Also consider enabling fallback to smaller compatible model variants for Hosted if error spikes continue (we’ve got the “burn spike -> fallback” rule in canary env but not prod-wide).

Miles Thornton: from the runbook, order is usually:
1) stop the bleeding (throttle / shed)
2) stabilize (route away / fallback)
3) then debug.
Given burn is already 14x/1h, I’d lean flipping protective throttling now to prevent cascading failures.

Cole Summers: I can flip `protective_throttling` in quota service for Hosted tier (per-route). It’ll reduce concurrency and enforce stricter rate limits temporarily.
Proposed config:
- tier=hosted
- routes: `/v1/chat/completions` + `/v1/completions` (streaming only)
- mode: `protective`
- target: cap at ~85% of current steady-state QPS (so we don’t slam the queue)
We can revert quickly.

Sean Gallagher: joining. What’s current customer impact? Any major escalations yet?

Owen Phillips: Support is seeing 3 tickets in the last ~15 min complaining about “stream stops mid-response” + “timeouts”. No named enterprise yet, mostly PLG.
If we’re going to shed load, would be good to get ahead of messaging (at least internal blurb for Support macros).

Aisha Bello: impact summary from dashboards:
- Hosted streaming p95 TTFT up from ~0.9s -> 3.8s (us-east-1)
- 5xx up to ~2.1% for route `/v1/chat/completions`
- streaming disconnect server-side rate ~1.6% (baseline <0.2%)
SLO burn: 30d budget remaining was ~38%, projected to drop fast if we don’t stabilize.

Mina Haddad: I can start a partial traffic shift now: move 15% of Hosted us-east-1 streaming to us-west-2, and 10% to eu-central-1 for EU traffic.
But if west tips over, we’ll just spread the fire.

Peter Holtz: agreed. Throttle first to stop queue blow-up.

Sean Gallagher: ok, decision: enable protective throttling (Hosted streaming only) + small routing shift after. Keep Dedicated untouched.
Miles/Aisha, please keep an eye on burn rates after the change.

Cole Summers: doing it. Rolling out config change now.
Command (for audit):
`quotactl set protective_throttling --tier=hosted --routes=/v1/chat/completions,/v1/completions --streaming_only=true --enabled=true --cap_percent=85 --ttl=60m`
(reactions: :white_check_mark: x4)

incident-bot: Update: Change detected
- Service: quota/throttling
- Action: `protective_throttling enabled` (tier=hosted, routes=/v1/chat/completions,/v1/completions, ttl=60m)
Owner: Cole Summers
Audit: https://admin.redwood.dev/audit/changes/ct-88917

Amara Diallo: gateway errors starting to trend down already (too early to call). 504s dropped ~15% over last 2 min.
Streaming disconnects still elevated but not climbing.

Mina Haddad: starting routing shift (small).
- 10% us-east-1 -> us-west-2 for Hosted streaming
- EU: 10% eu-west-1 -> eu-central-1
Will watch west capacity.

Ravi Menon: if disconnects remain high after throttling, we should check runtime “max stream duration” and any recent deploy. Did anything roll out in the last hour?

Aisha Bello: checking deploy history overlay… seeing a gateway canary promotion at ~20 min ago. Not sure it’s causal.
Link: https://grafana.redwood.dev/d/slo-hosted-overview?var-overlay=deploys
Also paging platform-oncall just in case we need rollback.

incident-bot: :pager: Page sent: platform-oncall
Reason: Hosted API SLO burn spike (streaming)
Incident: INC-2219

Peter Holtz: queue depth is coming down in us-east-1 (from ~42k -> 29k). GPU util still high but not pegged.
Looks like throttling is doing its job.

Miles Thornton: burn-rate panel:
- 1h burn now 11.0x (was 14.2x)
- 6h burn unchanged (expected)
We need to keep pushing it down below 10x to avoid paging loops.

Owen Phillips: can someone drop a 2-liner I can send to Support channel? Something like “mitigation in progress, expect intermittent timeouts/early disconnects for Hosted streaming, Dedicated unaffected”.

Sean Gallagher: yes. Owen, use:
“Mitigation in progress for Hosted streaming latency/timeouts (protective throttling + traffic shift). Dedicated capacity is not impacted. Next update in 15m; track INC-2219.”

Amara Diallo: additional data: 499s are up too but most look like client cancel while waiting for first token. That’s consistent w/ TTFT regression.
So improving TTFT should reduce both 499 + perceived disconnects.

Ravi Menon: could be cache churn or batch settings changed. But first stabilize.
If needed, we can temporarily prefer smaller fallback models for Hosted to reduce compute per token. That’s a bigger lever but has product implications.

Aisha Bello: agreed; let’s hold off fallback model until we see post-throttle steady state.
Also: Dedicated SLO dashboards are clean. No action there.

incident-bot: Metrics update (Hosted streaming, us-east-1)
- 5xx rate: 2.1% -> 1.4% (last 5m)
- p95 TTFT: 3.8s -> 2.6s (last 5m)
- server_disconnect: 1.6% -> 1.1% (last 5m)
SLO burn rate: 14.2x -> 9.7x (1h window)
(reactions: :chart_with_upwards_trend: x5)

Peter Holtz: nice. 1h burn <10x now.
We should keep throttling on for at least 30 min until queue fully clears, then reassess.

Mina Haddad: routing shift is stable; west is fine (+8% load). eu-central-1 absorbed EU shift w/out issues.

Miles Thornton: once stable, we should capture: “if protective throttling had been on earlier, burn would’ve stayed under threshold”. This is exactly the scenario we’re designing for.

Aisha Bello: +1. For now: monitoring. Next check-in 15 min.

incident-bot: Reminder: next incident update due in 15 minutes. Add notes in INC-2219: https://incidents.redwood.dev/inc/2219

Sean Gallagher: I’m going to step out unless we regress. Ping me if burn goes back up or if we need customer-facing comms.

Cole Summers: FYI throttling TTL is 60m. We can extend/shorten. Revert cmd:
`quotactl set protective_throttling --tier=hosted --routes=/v1/chat/completions,/v1/completions --streaming_only=true --enabled=false`

Amara Diallo: gateway graphs look much better now. remaining issue is elevated TTFT but it’s trending back.
I’ll dig into whether the earlier gateway promotion changed timeout defaults.

Aisha Bello: thanks all. keeping thread open for now; will post if anything changes.
